name: Prize crossword No 24,791

clue.text: Town of fortune for royal family?

blocks.note: hap is an old word for luck; 'of fortune' is read as fortune's, the possessive adding S
a burg is a town or borough

explanation.surface: Someone asks which lucky town a royal dynasty might choose to live in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town of fortune' is read as fortune's town, so the luck word with its 's comes first and the town after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hapsburgs were the ruling dynasty of Austria and Spain, a European royal house for centuries.

clue.text: Flushing it makes one psychologically aware

clue.text: Keep talking about Freetown in French

on as in 'a talk on' something, meaning about it

explanation.surface: Someone chattering endlessly about Sierra Leone's capital, but in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Freetown is the capital of Sierra Leone, a false trail; translate it into French and you get Libreville, capital of this West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Libreville, literally free town in French, is the capital city of this former French colony in central Africa.

clue.text: See 43

clue.text: Vagrant in hard times

clue.text: Student groups seize firm amid loud applause — they're up to the neck in revolution

explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to the neck in revolution' sounds like rebels deeply involved; read literally, these things sit up at the neck and turn over on themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll collar is a collar folded back on itself around the neckline, so it is turned over at the throat.

clue.text: Copper meets prosecutor on Scots island to fish

explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman beside the prosecutor, but it is the metal's symbol. In an across clue 'on' puts the island first.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a long predatory sea fish with sharp teeth, found in tropical waters.

clue.text: God's longing to return to Fenland abbey

a yen is a yearning

explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are the flat drained marshland of eastern England around Cambridgeshire, where several great abbeys stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorney Abbey is a Benedictine foundation near Peterborough, in the Cambridgeshire Fens, whose church survives.

clue.text: Western peak

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1952 cowboy film starring Gary Cooper
second meaning: the height or climax of something

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a mountain in the west; one sense is a classic film genre title, the other a figurative zenith.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a famous cowboy movie title and also means the culminating point, as the sun stands highest at midday.

clue.text: See 24

explanation.walkthrough: 'That' marks it as notorious: the Bullingdon is an exclusive Oxford dining club whose members included David Cameron and Boris Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bullingdon Club is a private, wealthy, all-male student dining society at Oxford University, known for rowdy dinners.

clue.text: Made fun of authority in Scots burgh

explanation.definitionFit: To joke is to say something in jest, and made fun is the matching past tense of that idea.

clue.text: Fish, boy, fish!

clue.text: A knight at the opera, said bogus Welshman

explanation.walkthrough: Taff, from the River Taff in Cardiff, is British slang for a Welshman. 'A Night at the Opera' is also the Marx Brothers film.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff, Shakespeare's fat knight, is the title character of Verdi's last opera, so he is a knight on the operatic stage.

clue.text: Trifles with society like a snake

clue.text: Between money and food there lives the philosopher

explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon the Elizabethan statesman wrote on scientific method; his namesake descendant was the Irish-born figurative painter.

clue.text: Former 18 member, missing on distinctive quality in it, has died: namely the black hole?
